claims.claim: Cyril of Alexandria was Patriarch of Alexandria from 412 to 444.
Cyril of Alexandria was born circa 375-376 and died in 444.
Theodore of Mopsuestia was Bishop of Mopsuestia in Cilicia for about 36 years and died in 428.

Theodore was a pupil of Diodore and his early controversy against the Arians and Apollinarians led him to speak of the Incarnation as though it were only a condescension of God the Son in connecting with Himself in some way a man who had an already distinct Being.
Cyril wrote Against Theodore of Mopsuestia to oppose Theodore's Christological views, which Cyril regarded as asserting 'two sons' rather than one Lord Jesus Christ.
The work survives only in fragments from books two and three, preserved in later collections.
The fragments were translated by P. E. Pusey and published in LFC 47 (1881) on pages 337-349 for book 2 and pages 350-362 for book 3.
Theodore's views were connected to the broader Antiochene Christological tradition that Cyril opposed, which Cyril found similar to the 'two sons' error.
